column2: My credit card company charged me a late fee even though I paid the bill two days early. I called twice and they keep saying the payment was not received on time. I want the fee removed.

I opened a checking account last spring and was promised there would be no monthly maintenance fee as long as I kept direct deposit. My paycheck has gone into that account every two weeks since then, but for the last three months the bank has taken a twelve dollar service charge anyway. When I asked a branch employee about it she said the promotion had ended, but nobody ever sent me a letter or an email saying the terms had changed. I would like the fees refunded and an explanation in writing.

Last month I sent money to my brother in another country using an online transfer service. The app showed the transfer as completed and took the money plus a fee from my debit card the same day. My brother went to the pickup location three times and was told there was nothing waiting for him. I contacted customer support through the chat and was told to wait five business days. After the five days I contacted them again and a different agent told me the transfer had been flagged for review and they needed more documents. I uploaded a copy of my identification and a recent utility bill the same afternoon. Since then I have heard nothing. It has now been almost four weeks. The money was meant to pay for my brother's rent and he is now behind. I have asked for either the transfer to be completed or a full refund including the fee, and every time I ask I am told someone will call me back within forty-eight hours, which never happens. I am filing this complaint because I do not know who else can help.

I am writing about the company that services my home loan. Two years ago I set up automatic payments from my savings account and they have gone through every month without a problem. In January the servicer told me my escrow account was short because my property taxes had gone up, and they raised my monthly payment by almost three hundred dollars. I checked with the county and my taxes actually went down slightly this year. I sent the servicer a copy of the tax bill from the county website and asked them to recalculate the escrow. They sent back a form letter saying the analysis was correct. I called and spent over an hour on hold, and the representative could not explain where the higher number came from. Meanwhile the higher payment has been taken from my account three times. I also noticed that a payment in March was applied to the principal instead of to the regular monthly installment, and now their website shows my loan as past due even though I paid the full amount. I am worried this will be reported and damage my credit, and I am also afraid of hearing the word foreclosure because I have never missed a payment. I want them to correct the escrow analysis, refund the overpayment, apply the March payment properly, and confirm in writing that my account is current.

For the past six months I have been receiving phone calls several times a day from a company that says I owe money on an old account. The first time they called they said the debt was from a store credit card, and the next time they said it was from a medical bill. I asked them to send me something in writing that shows what the debt is for and who the original creditor was, and they refused and said I had to pay first. They call my work number even though I told them I am not allowed to take personal calls at work, and one of their agents told my coworker that I was being sued. I have never been served with any court papers. I sent a letter by certified mail asking them to validate the debt and to stop calling me at work. They received the letter, according to the tracking, but the calls have continued and they have not sent any validation. Last week I pulled my credit report and found that this same company has added a collection account to my report with a balance that is higher than the amounts they mentioned on the phone. I disputed the item with the credit bureau, but the bureau says the company verified it. I do not recognize this debt, I have asked for proof more than once, and I believe the way they are contacting me is harassment. I want the calls to stop, I want proof of the debt, and I want the collection removed from my report until they can show it is mine. When I tried to explain this to the agent on the last call, he raised his voice, said that people like me always claim the debt is not theirs, and told me they would contact my family members if I did not set up a payment plan that day. I have kept a log of every call with the date, the time and the name the agent gave.

I am a small business owner and I took out a personal installment loan from an online lender eighteen months ago to cover equipment costs. The loan agreement said the interest rate was fixed and that there was no penalty for paying early. In the spring my business had a good quarter and I decided to pay off the remaining balance. I called the lender and asked for a payoff amount, and they gave me a figure over the phone. I paid that amount by bank transfer the next day and received an automated confirmation. Two weeks later I received a statement saying I still owed four hundred and sixty dollars, which they described as an early payoff fee and unpaid interest through the end of the original term. I sent them a copy of the agreement showing the no-prepayment-penalty clause and the confirmation of the payoff amount they gave me. They replied that the phone representative made a mistake and that the statement is correct. Since then they have added late charges to the balance every month and they have started sending emails saying the account will be sent to collections. I have also seen the account reported as delinquent on my credit file, which has already caused a problem when I applied to refinance my car loan with my credit union. I paid exactly what they told me to pay, I have the documents to prove it, and I want the remaining balance cancelled, the late charges removed and the negative reporting corrected. I have now spent many hours on the phone and writing letters about a balance that should be zero. Each time I call I am transferred between the billing team and the collections team, and each team says the other one has to fix it. One agent told me the only way to stop the late charges was to pay the disputed amount and then ask for a refund, which I am not willing to do because I do not owe it. I have kept copies of every letter, the original agreement, the bank transfer record and the confirmation number from the payoff call, and I am ready to provide them.
